correctness.rationale: For all n≥1 and both possible nonzero endpoint orbits, the kernel identity K_m(X,Y)=sum X_{0p}X_{qr}Y_{pq}Y_{rm} is proved. Square-free coordinate monomials are independent as Boolean functions. The two symmetry/cancellation cases yield exact rank n³−n²+n. The residual-Hankel theorem proves the upper bound; three explicit generator matrices produce the entire binary matrix monoid and therefore realize the lower rank exactly. Full matrix Hanks ranks 6 and 21 were independently recomputed for n=2 and 3, and a binary 6×6 minor was checked. Source minimality n follows from the unsquared full-monoid Hankel rank. Finite checks support but do not replace the all-dimension proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: An ordinary NFA accepts whenever at least one path exists, whereas an XNFA accepts when the number of paths is odd. The NFA theorem neither yields the strictly smaller parity upper bound nor establishes parity lower bounds. A general weighted-automaton Hankel minimization theorem is not an exact square-root rank calculation and does not imply the displayed polynomial without the new monomial-support analysis.

value.rationale: This is the exact all-parameter operational state complexity of a natural language operation under parity acceptance, rather than a narrow finite table. The polynomial n³−n²+n strictly improves the familiar n³ cubic cost at every n≥2, is attained over a fixed three-letter alphabet, and follows from a structural characteristic-two cancellation mechanism. It gives an explicit quantitative contrast between Boolean and GF(2) automata and certifies that the extremal sources really require n states.
